claims.title: Ancient peopling of the land
claims.summary: Hunter-gatherer peoples occupy the Pampas, Patagonia and the Andean northwest over many millennia, leaving sites such as the painted hands of the Cueva de las Manos.

sources.label: Cueva de las Manos, Rio Pinturas

claims.title: Diaguita and Guarani societies
claims.summary: Settled Diaguita farmers flourish in the northwest within the Andean world, while Guarani-speaking peoples cultivate the riverine northeast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1-diaguita-and-guarani-societies, claim TL:ARG:event:1:diaguita-and-guarani-societies, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spanish reach the Rio de la Plata
claims.summary: European expeditions begin to explore the great estuary of the Rio de la Plata, opening the region to Spanish ambitions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1516-spanish-reach-the-rio-de-la-plata, claim TL:ARG:event:1516:spanish-reach-the-rio-de-la-plata, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First founding of Buenos Aires
claims.summary: Pedro de Mendoza founds a first settlement on the Rio de la Plata, soon abandoned amid famine and Indigenous resistance, its survivors retreating to Asuncion.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1536-first-founding-of-buenos-aires, claim TL:ARG:event:1536:first-founding-of-buenos-aires, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Refounding of Buenos Aires
claims.summary: Juan de Garay leads an expedition from Asuncion and permanently re-establishes Buenos Aires, fixing the future capital on the estuary.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1580-refounding-of-buenos-aires, claim TL:ARG:event:1580:refounding-of-buenos-aires, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jesuit missions among the Guarani
claims.summary: The Jesuit Order founds mission towns among the Guarani that flourish until the order's expulsion from Spanish lands in 1767.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1609-jesuit-missions-among-the-guarani, claim TL:ARG:event:1609:jesuit-missions-among-the-guarani, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata created
claims.summary: Charles III establishes the new viceroyalty with Buenos Aires as capital, routing Potosi silver through the port and spurring its rise.

sources.label: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata

claims.title: Free trade reforms
claims.summary: Bourbon commercial reforms loosen Spain's trade monopoly, allowing Buenos Aires to trade more freely and accelerating its growth as an Atlantic port.

sources.label: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata

claims.title: British invasions repelled
claims.summary: British forces seize Buenos Aires twice and are twice expelled by local militias, kindling creole self-confidence and a taste for autonomy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1806-british-invasions-repelled, claim TL:ARG:event:1806:british-invasions-repelled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The May Revolution
claims.summary: An open cabildo in Buenos Aires deposes the viceroy and forms the Primera Junta, the first home government, launching the war of independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1810-the-may-revolution, claim TL:ARG:event:1810:the-may-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Belgrano raises the flag
claims.summary: Manuel Belgrano first flies the light-blue-and-white flag at Rosario; it is adopted by the Congress of Tucuman in 1816.

sources.label: Flag Day: Homage to General Manuel Belgrano

claims.summary: The Congress of Tucuman declares independence from Spain as the United Provinces of South America, signed by twenty-nine delegates under the presidency of Laprida.

claims.title: San Martin crosses the Andes
claims.summary: San Martin leads the Army of the Andes over the cordillera and defeats royalist forces at Chacabuco, opening the liberation of Chile.

claims.title: Collapse of central authority
claims.summary: The United Provinces fragment as central government breaks down and provincial caudillos contend for power, beginning decades of civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1820-collapse-of-central-authority, claim TL:ARG:event:1820:collapse-of-central-authority, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The rule of Rosas
claims.summary: The Federalist caudillo Juan Manuel de Rosas dominates Argentina as governor of Buenos Aires until his fall, a period of strongman rule and conflict.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1829-the-rule-of-rosas, claim TL:ARG:event:1829:the-rule-of-rosas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Caseros
claims.summary: Justo Jose de Urquiza defeats Rosas at Caseros, opening the way to the constitutional organisation of the country.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1852-battle-of-caseros, claim TL:ARG:event:1852:battle-of-caseros, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: A constituent congress at Santa Fe sanctions the Constitution of 1853, establishing a federal, representative and republican state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1853-the-national-constitution, claim TL:ARG:event:1853:the-national-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Conquest of the Desert
claims.summary: Military campaigns led by Julio Argentino Roca seize the Pampas and northern Patagonia from the Mapuche and other peoples through killing, subjugation and displacement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1878-the-conquest-of-the-desert, claim TL:ARG:event:1878:the-conquest-of-the-desert, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mass European immigration
claims.summary: Some four million immigrants, chiefly Italians and Spaniards, arrive to settle and work the land, so that by 1914 nearly a third of Argentines are foreign-born.

claims.title: First election under universal male suffrage
claims.summary: Hipolito Yrigoyen of the Radical Civic Union wins the presidency in the first vote under the secret universal male ballot of 1912.

claims.summary: Amid the Great Depression the army overthrows Yrigoyen, opening the fraud-ridden Infamous Decade and a century of military intervention.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1930-the-first-military-coup, claim TL:ARG:event:1930:the-first-military-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Juan Peron wins the presidency with broad working-class support, launching the Peronist movement that will dominate Argentine politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1946-peron-elected-president, claim TL:ARG:event:1946:peron-elected-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peron overthrown
claims.summary: The Revolucion Libertadora ousts Peron, who goes into an exile of nearly two decades while Peronism is banned at home.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1955-peron-overthrown, claim TL:ARG:event:1955:peron-overthrown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peron's return and death
claims.summary: Peron returns from exile and is re-elected president in 1973, but dies on 1 July 1974, leaving power to his wife Isabel amid deepening crisis.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1973-peron-s-return-and-death, claim TL:ARG:event:1973:peron-s-return-and-death, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Military coup and the Dirty War
claims.summary: The armed forces seize power and launch the National Reorganization Process, a dictatorship whose Dirty War forcibly disappears thousands of people; from 1977 the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo march weekly to demand their return.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1976-military-coup-and-the-dirty-war, claim TL:ARG:event:1976:military-coup-and-the-dirty-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Falklands/Malvinas War
claims.summary: Argentina invades the Falklands/Malvinas on 2 April; after ten weeks of war its forces surrender to Britain on 14 June, discrediting the junta.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1982-the-falklands-malvinas-war, claim TL:ARG:event:1982:the-falklands-malvinas-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to democracy
claims.summary: Raul Alfonsin is inaugurated president, restoring civilian democratic rule after seven years of dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Argentina: From the Diaguita, Guarani and Mapuche worlds of the Rio de la Plata to a Spanish viceroyalty, the independence declared at Tucuman in 1816, an age of mass immigration, the Peron era, and a hard road back to democracy after the dictatorship of 1976-1983.", terralore.co/country/ARG/chronicle#ev-1983-return-to-democracy, claim TL:ARG:event:1983:return-to-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.summary: Following the CONADEP report Nunca Mas, civilian courts try and convict the junta leaders for the crimes of the Dirty War.

claims.summary: A severe financial collapse forces a sovereign default and topples several presidents in days, the gravest crisis of the democratic era.
